# PR #755 review feedback: drop the initrd-Bluetooth machinery

You are on PR #755's branch (weller refresh). The owner reviewed and ruled:
the Bluetooth-at-LUKS-prompt setup carried over from the old config never
actually worked (history: added in #280, reverted in #283, re-added in #329,
"improved" in #331, then the machine died — no evidence of success), and on
the new X870E hardware it's harder still (MediaTek WiFi-7/BT combo firmware in
initrd, pairing keys that don't exist until after install, keys stored
unencrypted on the ESP). Remove it rather than carry it forward.

## Changes

1. In `hosts/weller/hardware.nix`: remove the entire initrd-Bluetooth block —
   the bluez initrd packages/dbus service, the btusb/bluetooth/uhid/hidp/
   hid_generic initrd kernel modules, the `boot.initrd.secrets`
   `/var/lib/bluetooth` entry, the initrd bluetooth main.conf contents, and
   any install-safety guard the current PR added around those secrets.
   KEEP `boot.initrd.systemd.enable` itself if other parts rely on it (it's
   fine on its own), and keep normal post-boot Bluetooth untouched (that
   comes from the common modules, not this file).
2. In `docs/weller-build-2026.md`: replace any Bluetooth-pairing/initrd-BT
   post-install steps with one line: LUKS passphrase at boot is typed on a
   USB keyboard; the Kinesis pairs normally once booted.
3. Nothing else. Do not touch other hosts or modules.

## Acceptance

- `nix flake check` passes — paste final lines.
- `nix build --dry-run .#nixosConfigurations.weller.config.system.build.toplevel`
  evaluates; `weller-bootstrap` still evaluates.
- `git diff --stat` for this commit in the report.
- Commit to the current branch and push (updates PR #755). Do not open a new
  PR, do not merge.
